records.title: Gallup: Obama job approval mid-June 2012 (public summary)
records.provenance: Gallup public tracking summaries, June 2012. Attributed aggregate, not a SHORTLIST or psbx claim about any person.
records.text: Gallup's public mid-June 2012 tracking summary put President Obama's job approval near 46 percent, with disapproval near 47 percent. Independents remained split. The figures are contemporaneous published toplines as of 2012-06-17, not later revised series.

records.title: Gallup generic congressional ballot, June 2012 (public summary)
records.provenance: Gallup public summaries, June 2012. Attributed aggregate.
records.text: Gallup's June 2012 public generic-ballot summaries showed a close national House race, with neither party holding a large durable lead among registered voters. Treat as an attributed contemporaneous topline, not a precinct forecast.

records.title: Pew: party identification, early June 2012 (public summary)
records.provenance: Pew Research Center public political typology / party ID summaries, 2012. Attributed aggregate.
records.text: Pew's publicly summarized 2012 party-identification series described a closely divided electorate, with large independent and leaner groups. Party ID remained a stable long-term orientation in the published commentary. This is an attributed summary of public Pew material as of early June 2012.

records.title: RCP national presidential average, late June 2012 (public summary)
records.provenance: RealClearPolitics public poll average, late June 2012. Attributed aggregate of published polls.
records.sample_note: Average of published national polls; not microdata
records.text: Public poll averages in late June 2012 showed a close Obama–Romney national race, within a few points either way depending on the house effects of the component polls. This is an attributed contemporaneous summary of published averages, not a later election result.
